It solves the problem of interactive exploration of volumetric datasets by decoupling the rendering logic into modular shader components (vertex, classification, gradient, lighting, and shadow) that can be linked and modified at runtime [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the framework uses a 'single-pass GPU ray casting' implementation where the rendering pipeline is customizable via 'interactive shader editing'. It details that the fragment shader implementation consists of several separate files (classify.fs, grad.fs, light.fs, shadow.fs) alongside the main entry point, which aligns with the claim of 'modular shader components'. The ability to 'browse, load and attach' these shaders and the fact that linking succeeds when all components are attached supports the idea that they can be linked and modified. While the text describes the workflow of attaching shaders rather than explicitly using the phrase 'decoupling... at runtime', the functionality described (interactive editing, separate modular files, attaching/detaching) supports the claim that the logic is decoupled into these components for interactive exploration.

*   **Linking Failure:** The pipeline will not produce ray-cast output if any of the required fragment shader files (`classify.fs`, `grad.fs`, `light.fs`, `shadow.fs`) are missing from the attachment list [S1].

The claim states that the pipeline will not produce ray-cast output if any of the required fragment shader files are missing. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'As soon as all of the above shader files are attached, linking will succeed.' It also notes that 'Linking succeeds only when all specified shader files (vertex and all fragment components) are attached.' Furthermore, it clarifies that 'the full ray casting implementation requires shader attachment,' whereas MIP and SLICING do not. Since linking is a prerequisite for the shader pair to function, and linking fails if components are missing, the evidence supports the claim that the ray-cast output (which relies on the linked shader pair) will not be produced if the required files are missing.
